sentences.text: Pelecanimimus was a small ornithomimosaur measuring about 1.9 to 2.5 meters in length and weighing 17 to 30 kilograms.
The only known specimen is an articulated front half of a skeleton including the skull, jaws, neck vertebrae, most back vertebrae, ribs, sternum, pectoral girdle, and parts of the forelimbs.
This animal had approximately 220 very small teeth in total, distributed across the premaxilla, maxilla, and dentary, displaying two distinct basic forms.
All of its teeth were unserrated and had a narrow waist between them.
Pelecanimimus lacked interdental plates.
Its skull is long, narrow, and pointed, with a maximum length nearly 4.5 times its height, large eyes, and a crest on the back of the head.
Pelecanimimus possessed a unique adaptation of having a large number of teeth interpreted as a functional counterpart to a beak's cutting edge.
A mysterious pouch similar to that of modern pelicans was found, though its function remains unknown.
Armando Díaz Romeral discovered a Pelecanimimus skeleton at the Las Hoyas Unit 3 site in July 1993.
Pelecanimimus polyodon was named and described in 1994 by a team including Bernardino Pérez-Moreno and José Luis Sanz.
The generic name derives from the Latin pelecanus, meaning "pelican," and mimus, meaning "mimic," referring to the long snout and throat pouch.
The holotype specimen of Pelecanimimus, LH777, is currently located in the Museo Paleontológico de Castilla-La Mancha in Cuenca, Spain, and was recovered from lagerstätte beds.
Pelecanimimus was determined to be omnivorous, capable of stripping foliage or hunting lizards.
Because its remains were found along a lake, it is hypothesized that the animal used its pouch for fishing.
Pelecanimimus is the first discovered ornithomimosaur where the hyoid apparatus, a group of specialized neck bones, has been preserved.
A 2026 study by Calvo-Pérez & Cuesta reports evidence that the endocranial morphology of Pelecanimimus polyodon is similar to that of other ornithomimosaurs.
A phylogenetic analysis by Makovicky et al. (2005) indicates that Pelecanimimus is the most primitive member of Ornithomimosauria, less derived than Harpymimus.
Pelecanimimus lived in Spain during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, about 125 million years ago, during the Barremian.
Pelecanimimus lived during the Barremian stage, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
Its habitat of temperate forests and humid climates allowed it to live among abundant food sources.
Despite being an ornithomimosaur, it may have been one of the main predators in its area.
The fossil-bearing levels belong to the finely laminated limestones of the Rambla de Las Cruces II unit, deposited during the Late Barremian.
It is debated whether the evolution of toothlessness in ornithomimosaurs resulted from progressive reduction or an exaptation process involving an increase in tooth number.
